design_judgment.intended_result: Both candidates state an explicit intended user result, reader decision, and material design choice, and the bodies match those statements. Source Architecture 02 promises that a maintainer can place or split a source unit, decide legal imports and exports, distinguish Runtime product code from repository support planes, and judge implementation eligibility without reading a manually maintained file inventory; sections 2 through 9 deliver exactly that through four code-owned manifests plus a ten-item conformance list. Registry 01 promises that a maintainer can determine what Runtime versions, which source change creates a new release, and how one Skill source exports multiple independently owned Modules; sections 2 through 7 deliver release identity law, seven owns/does-not-own release families, bundle-as-transport, and a five-decision lifecycle split. The two reader gains are mutually consistent: Registry section 11 item 9 defers its public namespace to the Source Architecture manifest rather than restating it. One residual defect: activation, the decision that produces Registry's most visible product result, is keyed on a 'declared Registry scope' that no candidate, the T1 root, or the Runtime T0 ever defines.
design_judgment.authority_structure: Layer, owner, parent, and owned object are valid for both candidates. Each declares layer T2, canonical_owner matching its own target path, and parent designDoc/agent_runtime_00_runtime_domain_contract.md; the agent_runtime_ prefix mechanically binds both to that unique T1 root, satisfying Design Doc Management section 2.3, and both appear in the root candidate's specialization_contracts list. The owned objects are disjoint from each other and from the root: 'Agent Runtime source ownership and dependency architecture', 'immutable Agent Runtime release identity and dependency closure', and 'independently governed Agent Runtime domain'. Revision 1 finding f01 is genuinely closed: section 3 rule 6, section 6, and conformance item 4 bind T2 03 Event Ingress and T2 09 External Authority Integration source and public contracts to Execution, the diagram folds them into the Execution node, and no seventh responsibility, competing source-owner class, or peer public namespace is created. This is consistent with T1 section 2, which already classes 03 and 09 as specializations that create no additional peers, and with T1's delegation of the exact machine-checked import graph and public-surface manifest to document 02. The known namespace-owner collisions over canonical filenames 02, 05, and 10 are not claimed closed: the review brief states the review does not waive the re-home prerequisites and the manifest lists 'Agency Platform and Software Delivery still claim Runtime-prefixed 02, 10, and 05 contracts' as an adoption blocker, which Software Delivery's own owned_specialization_contracts entry for agent_runtime_05_delivery_roadmap.md confirms. They are therefore reported here only as unresolved declared blockers, not duplicated as candidate-body findings.
design_judgment.boundary_coherence: Semantic owner, author, operator, reviewer, persistence owner, implementation binding, and approval authority remain distinguishable in both candidates. Source Architecture section 4 assigns ownership 'by the behavior and state transition it implements, not by its current directory, filename, imported technology, or storage location', which directly refuses the directory-as-owner defect named in Design Doc Management section 6; section 7 labels the five repository planes as planes rather than peer responsibilities; section 10 separates the validator's reporting role from repair and from Software Delivery's release decision, and states that an AI reviewer cannot waive a deterministic failure. Revision 1 finding f02 is closed: the section 3 diagram now carries three labeled subgraphs for Runtime product responsibilities, the supporting source class, and the build and conformance tooling plane. Registry keeps record meaning and intended writer semantics with Registry, System-of-Record and writer-boundary binding with Data Governance, migration code and deployment with Software Delivery, and lifecycle permission with Product Authorization, and section 11 item 7 holds admission, activation, deactivation, withdrawal, host selection, and Product Authorization apart as distinct decisions. No duplicated ownership, approval, admission, or canonical-write authority was found, and no unlike dimensions are presented as peer responsibilities.
design_judgment.inheritance_and_dependencies: Dependency direction closes in the normal case. The Source Architecture graph has no reverse peer edge, requires composition in Execution or external host assembly rather than mutual imports, keeps concrete adapters depending inward on their own responsibility's port, and forbids build and conformance tooling from being imported by execution code. Registry's declared dependencies match: section 8 states Registry declares no dependency on the External Authority Integration ports, section 11 item 8 forbids importing an authoring tree, provider implementation, Durability implementation, Execution state, or business database, and section 8 keeps Durability graph types out of the returned surface, which resolves the Registry-to-Invocation and Registry-to-Durability cycles recorded in the code architecture audit. Timestamp inheritance closes twice as required: Source Architecture section 5 bounds foundation instant validation to format, precision, and ordering and denies it a protected predicate or cross-clock decision, matching Timestamp Semantics sections 6.7 and 8 (f06 closed); Registry section 9 binds every persisted record family to Timestamp Semantics with store-assigned recorded_at_utc and an exact per-class registration, matching Timestamp Semantics sections 2 and 4 (f08 closed), and states the startup-mutation rule store-neutrally with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS as an explicit example only. Two inheritance gaps remain. Registry imposes Data Governance obligations in sections 9 and 11 while omitting designDoc/the_data_governance.md from its declared inherits closure. More materially, the f07 mechanism of accepting an already-resolved decision ref leaves no named enforcement point: Registry verifies only that a ref was supplied, and Product Authorization section 5 obligations to validate the current decision and resolve action, resource, and context server-side are consumed by no document in the set.
design_judgment.intent_code_separation: Stable intent is cleanly separated from mutable implementation truth in both candidates. Neither names a current source path, file or line count, provider, model, database product, durable backend, package version, test result, or delivery status; Source Architecture's non_goals exclude 'current source-file inventory, line counts, versions, implementation status, or delivery plan' and Registry's exclude 'current releases, active pointers, provider bindings, database product, or migration status'. Source Architecture section 2 delegates exact paths, symbols, exception IDs, hashes, current violations, and generated views to code-owned registrations and rejects a prose list, an unregistered directory scan, or a magic file count as substitutes, which answers the magic-count defect recorded in the code architecture audit. Migration debt is an exact registered set with owner, disposition, entry basis, and exit evidence, compared by identity rather than aggregate count, so debt cannot be silently reset to the current tree. Revision 1 findings f03, f04, and f05 are closed as exact rules rather than descriptions: the package root exports package metadata only and no responsibility record, protocol, service, error, Adapter, or implementation type; repository plane is a recorded field of RuntimeSourceOwnershipManifest and a conformance item; and conformance item 7 keeps architecture-owned projection parity separate from the T2 05 Design Contract bundle parity that T1 section 13 assigns to document 05. Registry's SQL and capability examples are framed as illustrations of a store-neutral or provider-neutral rule, consistent with Design Doc Management section 3.
design_judgment.implementability: An implementer could form a Code Design Basis for architecture enforcement and for most of Registry from these two documents, and the next Ledger, Invocation, and Durability candidates can consume the resulting seams without inventing a missing peer. Three things still force invention. First, activation cannot be implemented as specified: 'Registry scope' is undefined across the candidate set, and section 11 contains no conformance item proving at most one active release per scope, so an implementer must invent both the activation key and its uniqueness rule, with a real risk of importing host or tenant routing that Registry's own non_goals forbid. Second, the lifecycle authorization path forces the implementer to invent authority, because the only stated caller obligation is that a ref was supplied and the only external caller reachable under the Source Architecture graph is a host or operator surface outside the Runtime import graph. Third, the section 3 diagram is presented as 'the allowed logical direction' yet grants EXECUTION an edge to the foundation while omitting the same edge for INSPECTION; section 3 rule 1 resolves this in favour of every responsibility, but the diagram and the encoded RuntimeDependencyPolicy would disagree if read literally. Separately, the frozen subject package is not reproducible: it carries a prose paraphrase of the revision 1 findings instead of their identities and dispositions, and binds no hash for the inherited T0 authorities both capsules declare, so a later reviewer cannot resolve the same closure without out-of-band material.

findings.quoted_evidence: Product Authorization owns the lifecycle permission decision. The Registry writer verifies that the caller supplied the required opaque decision ref, records that ref with the lifecycle fact, and neither evaluates, issues, nor widens it. Registry declares no dependency on the External Authority Integration ports.
findings.requirement: Product Authorization section 5 makes the resource-owning service or Gateway the Policy Enforcement Point and requires it to 'resolve the exact action, resource, tenant, Cell, and trusted context' and to 'obtain or validate the current Product Authorization decision'. Section 4 requires each resource-owning service to publish a code-owned ResourcePermissionManifest with its resource types, atomic actions, scope forms, and grant requirement class. Section 9 declares the design non-conformant when 'a caller-selected Principal, tenant, Cell, action, resource, or context is trusted without server-side resolution' or when 'a resource operation executes without a current decision or the required high-risk grant'.
findings.impact: Activation, deactivation, and withdrawal are canonical-write decisions over which admitted release is current, and the only caller reachable for them under the Source Architecture graph is an external host or operator surface. As written, the sole authorization evidence is that the caller attached a syntactically present opaque ref: nothing in the candidate set validates that the decision is current, unrevoked, unexpired, and issued for this exact lifecycle action and release resource, and no peer document is named as the enforcement point that performs that validation before the call. Registry section 10 codifies the presence-only rule by rejecting only a lifecycle command that lacks a ref. An implementer must therefore invent the enforcement authority, and the natural implementation is a default-allow canonical mutation, which Product Authorization section 9 names as non-conformant. Correctly closing f07 by removing the 09 port dependency did not by itself close the inherited enforcement obligation.
findings.accountable_owner_ref: designDoc/agent_runtime_01_registry_contract.md canonical_owner — Runtime Registry T2 design owner, accepted by the Project Owner or delegated design owner per designDoc/the_design_doc_management.md section 9
findings.required_change: In Registry section 8, state which boundary enforces the lifecycle decision, without importing the T2 09 ports. Either declare the Registry writer to be the Policy Enforcement Point for Registry lifecycle resources and require it to resolve and validate the current authorization decision server-side against the exact requested action and release resource per Product Authorization section 5, and require Registry to publish its own ResourcePermissionManifest naming the activation, deactivation, and withdrawal actions and their grant requirement class; or name the external enforcement point that must perform that validation and state explicitly that Registry is not the Policy Enforcement Point. Then extend section 10 with failure rows for an expired, revoked, or non-matching decision ref, and add a section 11 conformance item proving that a lifecycle mutation is refused when the supplied decision does not currently authorize that exact action and resource.

findings.quoted_evidence: The Registry writer does not activate a release merely because admission passes. Admission means valid for Runtime use. Activation selects one current release for one declared Registry scope. Deactivation removes that selection without changing the admitted release.
findings.requirement: Design Doc Management section 6.1 requires that the design guide implementation 'without forcing the reviewer to redesign it or infer missing authority', and section 2.3 forbids a T2 from widening its parent's semantic authority. Registry's own non_goals exclude 'Product Authorization, host routing, domain acceptance, or software release admission', and section 11 item 7 requires activation and host selection to remain distinct decisions.
findings.impact: 'Registry scope' is the key on which activation, deactivation, and the meaning of 'which release is active' all depend, and it is defined nowhere in either candidate, in the revision 7 T1 root, or in the Runtime T0 that also uses the phrase. An implementer must invent both the scope key and its uniqueness rule. Section 11 contains no conformance item proving that at most one release is active per scope, so the single most important invariant of a current-release pointer is unprovable from the contract. The plausible inventions — per tenant, per host, per environment, or per deployment — would pull host routing or Product Authorization dimensions into Registry, contradicting Registry's declared non_goals and the separation required by section 11 item 7.
findings.accountable_owner_ref: designDoc/agent_runtime_01_registry_contract.md canonical_owner — Runtime Registry T2 design owner, accepted by the Project Owner or delegated design owner per designDoc/the_design_doc_management.md section 9
findings.required_change: Define Registry scope in section 7 at intent level: state which semantic dimensions a scope may contain, state explicitly that it contains no tenant, host, product-route, environment, or deployment identity, and leave the exact field set to code-owned schemas. Add the uniqueness invariant that at most one release is active per (release family, scope) at any time, and add a matching section 11 conformance item and a section 10 failure row for an activation that would create a second current selection in one scope.

findings.requirement: Design Doc Management section 6 requires design audit to check 'peer-boundary and inherited-constraint closure', and invariant 3 requires a contract to name its inherited constraints. Registry section 9 and section 11 item 10 impose Data Governance obligations directly: 'Data Governance registers the Registry record families as managed Data Assets and binds the one System of Record and writer boundary' and 'every persisted Registry class has its required Timestamp and Data Asset registrations', which are the DataAssetRegistration, StorageBinding, and DataMigrationRegistration laws of designDoc/the_data_governance.md sections 3 and 4.5.
findings.impact: Registry is the only persistent-record owner in this dependency slice, and Data Governance is the T0 that binds its System of Record, writer boundary, forward and rollback migration transitions, and rollback window. The declared inherits list is the closure a machine inheritance check reads, and it selectively names Product Authorization and Timestamp Semantics while omitting the one T0 that governs the obligations Registry actually states in sections 9 and 11. A later change to Data Governance migration or writer-boundary law would not be flagged as affecting Registry, and the candidate's own conformance items would be validated against an incomplete declared closure.

findings.required_change: Add designDoc/the_data_governance.md to the Registry Contract Capsule inherits list so the declared inheritance closure matches the Data Governance obligations already stated in sections 9 and 11, and confirm that designDoc/the_software_delivery.md is either declared or that its section 9 and section 12 references are restated as peer handoffs rather than inherited constraints.

findings.quoted_evidence: The first T2 advisory review blocked revision 1 on an incomplete source-owner class for T2 03 and T2 09 implementations, plus seven bounded inheritance, public-surface, projection, and persistence findings. Revision 2 binds both specialization implementations to Execution, labels repository planes, closes Product Authorization and Timestamp inheritance, and narrows each conformance owner without creating another Runtime responsibility.
findings.requirement: Contract Audit section 7 requires that 'when the immediate predecessor version of the same subject identity has unresolved actionable findings, the successor subject closure must carry all of them as immutable declared inputs. The subject owner cannot omit or select a subset. The reviewer must disposition every carried finding and cannot recover additional history from memory or ambient records.' Section 7 further states that 'a missing or unresolved actionable predecessor finding blocks a passing result.'
findings.impact: The frozen revision 2 package carries a prose paraphrase of the revision 1 result in the review brief and lists no predecessor finding identities, texts, severities, or claimed dispositions anywhere in subject_manifest.json. The eight findings verified in this review reached the reviewer only through the out-of-band review request, which is exactly the ambient-history channel Contract Audit forbids. As a result the closure of f01 through f08 cannot be independently reproduced from the subject package, and a future reviewer of the same subject identity could not confirm that no revision 1 finding was silently dropped.

findings.required_change: Add a predecessor-finding closure section to subject_manifest.json that carries every actionable revision 1 finding as an immutable declared input: finding identity, severity, affected candidate, correction target, and the claimed disposition with the exact revision 2 section that closes it. findings.requirement: Design Doc Management section 6.1 defines the Design Contract review subject as containing 'the complete candidate Design Intent set' together with 'the applicable Charter, parent, peer, dependency, and inherited-constraint closure', and section 3 requires an exact review subject to bind content hashes so that a changed input invalidates the in-flight subject.
findings.impact: The two candidates declare seven distinct inherited or consumed T0 authorities across their capsules and bodies — Charter, Agent Runtime, Timestamp Semantics, Product Authorization, Data Governance, Skill Governance, Software Delivery, and Design Doc Management — but subject_manifest.json binds hashes for only three inputs, none of which is a designDoc/the_*.md authority. The revision 7 root manifest by contrast does bind designDoc/the_design_doc_management.md by hash. Judging f06, f07, and f08 required reading the unhashed Timestamp Semantics, Product Authorization, and Data Governance texts, so the review closure actually used is wider than the frozen subject and a later re-review could silently resolve a different version of the governing law.

findings.requirement: Section 2 assigns RuntimeDependencyPolicy the duty to declare 'the exact allowed responsibility and foundation edges', section 3 introduces the diagram as 'The allowed logical direction is', and conformance item 2 requires that 'every import edge is permitted and the responsibility graph is acyclic'.
findings.impact: The revision 2 diagram adds EXECUTION --> FOUNDATION, correctly absorbing the former ingress and authority nodes, but leaves Inspection as the only responsibility with no foundation edge. Section 3 rule 1 resolves the ambiguity by granting every responsibility the foundation import, so this does not block implementation, but a policy encoded literally from the diagram would deny Inspection the canonical serialization, instant validation, and content-reference primitives it needs and would reproduce the duplicated-primitive defect the foundation exists to remove.

Both restatements are currently faithful, so no rule is widened, but the undeclared closure means a later change to either governing T0 would not be mechanically flagged as affecting this contract.

safe_next_step: Return findings f09 through f15 to their named correction targets and re-freeze a revision 3 subject; do not admit, implement, or regenerate anything from revision 2. The smallest safe sequence is: (1) the Runtime Registry T2 design owner corrects f09, f10, and f11 inside agent_runtime_01_registry_contract.md by naming the lifecycle enforcement point and its Product Authorization section 5 obligations without importing the T2 09 ports, defining Registry scope and its per-scope activation uniqueness invariant with matching conformance and failure entries, and adding designDoc/the_data_governance.md to the declared inherits closure; (2) the Source Architecture T2 design owner applies the two note-level corrections f14 and f15; (3) the subject owner corrects f12 and f13 by carrying revision 1 findings f01 through f08 with their dispositions and revision 2 findings f09 through f15 as immutable declared inputs, and by binding every inherited T0 authority in the manifest by path and sha256. Revision 1 findings f01 through f08 are verified closed and need no further work: 03 and 09 source and public contracts are bound to Execution with no new responsibility or source-owner class, the diagram separates the three node classes, the package root export rule is closed rather than vague, repository plane is a registered manifest field and conformance item, architecture projection parity is separated from T2 05 bundle parity, foundation instant validation is bounded by Timestamp Semantics and denied any protected predicate, Registry lifecycle takes an already-resolved decision ref with no authority-port dependency, and persisted Registry families inherit Timestamp Semantics under a store-neutral startup-mutation rule. The declared adoption blockers remain open and are not addressed by this result: the peer-owner re-home of the Runtime-prefixed 02, 05, and 10 filenames, the missing independent T2 verdict, and the Runtime review host that still imports the retired registry_module_exporting interface. Because that host is broken, this remains advisory evidence under Contract Audit section 5 bootstrap semantics and cannot be recorded as a Runtime-executed admission result or substitute for the fixed design_contract_reviewer binding.
